[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Tutorial: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Pooling in Deep Learning"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are a specialized class of artificial neural networks designed for processing grid-like data, such as images. Unlike traditional fully connected networks, CNNs leverage spatial hierarchies through local connectivity and parameter sharing."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Convolutional Layer"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The core building block of a CNN is the convolutional layer. It applies a set of learnable filters (or kernels) across the input image. Each filter slides over the spatial dimensions, computing element-wise multiplications and summing the results to produce a feature map."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# Define a simple convolutional layer
# In channels = 3 (RGB), Out channels = 16, Kernel size = 3x3
conv_layer = nn.Conv2d(in_channels=3, out_channels=16, kernel_size=3, stride=1, padding=1)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Hyperparameters of Convolutions"},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Kernel Size: Determines the receptive field of the filters, typically 3x3 or 5x5."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Stride: The step size at which the filter moves across the input. A higher stride reduces spatial dimensions."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Padding: Adding zeros around the border of the input to preserve spatial dimensions and control output size."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"The Role of Pooling Layers"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Pooling layers are inserted periodically between convolutional layers to progressively reduce the spatial size (width and height) of the representation. This helps decrease the amount of parameters and computation in the network, while also controlling overfitting."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Types of Pooling"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Max Pooling: Extracts the maximum value from the region covered by the filter. It highlights dominant features like edges."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Average Pooling: Computes the average value of the region covered by the filter, providing a smoother downsampling approach."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"# Define a Max Pooling layer
max_pool = nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=2, stride=2)

# Define an Average Pooling layer
avg_pool = nn.AvgPool2d(kernel_size=2, stride=2)"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Putting It Together in PyTorch"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"A standard feature extraction block in a CNN typically consists of a convolutional layer, a non-linear activation function (like ReLU), followed by a pooling layer."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"class SimpleCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super(SimpleCNN, self).__init__()
        self.feature_extractor = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 32, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=2, stride=2),
            nn.Conv2d(32, 64, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=2, stride=2)
        )
        
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.feature_extractor(x)
        return x"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"By stacking these convolutional and pooling blocks, CNNs can automatically learn hierarchical feature representations, ranging from low-level edges and textures in early layers to high-level semantic shapes in deeper layers."}]
